title: Deployable contact pipeline: hosted Postgres + real email delivery
description:
Made the contact form deployable by removing its two blockers: the site ran on a local SQLite file, and Resend was never wired, so every note sat in the table with emailedAt null. Both are now real services. Postgres is hosted at Neon, provisioned through Stripe Projects into its own `nadia-website` project rather than the pre-existing `fun-site` project, which already held an unrelated database and a Vercel link the user identified as wrong. Email delivery goes through Customer.io's transactional API. Verified end to end against both live services: HTTP 201, row persisted to Neon, emailedAt stamped at 2026-08-27T21:24:33.610Z, and a real message delivered with a returned delivery_id.

The pipeline was then decomposed. POST /api/contact had inlined five responsibilities across 58 lines with three try/catch blocks; it now reads as six named steps composing tested units. The extraction that mattered most was deliverAndStamp, which owns the ordering rule: emailedAt is stamped strictly AFTER the provider accepts, never before and never on a failed send, because emailedAt is the only record of whether a note reached the inbox and stamping optimistically would make an undelivered note indistinguishable from a delivered one. Its collaborators are arguments rather than imports, so all three outcomes — delivered, not-delivered, delivered-unstamped — are reachable without a database or a mail provider. A second extraction, prismaConnection, hoisted the DATABASE_URL guard that app/lib/prisma.ts and prisma/seed.ts had been duplicating; seed.ts's own header comment had been asking the next reader to keep the two in sync, which is a request, not enforcement. The dependency graph now shows both entry points importing the shared helper.

The suite went from 36 to 93 tests, all passing, with the audit clean at 0 findings.

Four things are worth carrying forward. First, Stripe Projects' Customer.io integration does NOT provision an App API key; the NADIA_MAIL_SITE_ID / NADIA_MAIL_API_KEY pair are Track API credentials that authenticate against track.customer.io and are rejected by the send endpoint. The working credential is the sa_sandbox_* service-account token, exposed to the app as CUSTOMERIO_SEND_TOKEN via `stripe projects variables set`. An earlier conclusion in this session that no send credential existed was wrong: it generalized from 401s on /v1/campaigns and /v1/segments, which the sandbox token is simply not scoped for, to the send endpoint, which it does work on. Second, `stripe projects init` writes AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md unless --skip-skills is passed; those are this repo's codeyam instruction files, and their checksums were verified unchanged afterwards. Third, the seed helpers had to move to prisma/seedRows.ts rather than staying in seed.ts, because seed.ts calls main() at module scope — a test importing a helper from it would have connected to the database and run deleteMany, wiping the developer's table as a side effect of the import. Fourth, `stripe projects config-override` echoes the value it writes, so the Neon connection string including its password was printed into the session transcript; the user was told and chose to leave the credential rather than rotate it.

One environmental limitation, unresolved and not caused by this feature: the codeyam preview cannot reach the database. The editor injects PGHOST=127.0.0.1 and PGPORT=14252 into the dev server to route database traffic through its own proxy, but nothing ever listens on 14252, so in-preview form submissions hang for 60s instead of failing fast. Restarting both the editor and the dev server did not bring the proxy up. The feature was therefore verified at the route level and against the live services instead, which is why the Demo step showed no browser interaction. Configuring `database` in editor.local.json required a DatabaseConfig object whose `originalUrl` field is undocumented and was inferred; it parses and the capture-DB name derives correctly, but that inference should be confirmed against codeyam-editor source before it is relied on.

Redness proof, stated as recorded rather than as remembered: `does not stamp when the provider rejects the send` is AGENT-ATTESTED by hand, NOT tool-measured — prove-red BLOCKED with the without-fix world failing to build, since reverting the module deletes the symbols the test imports. Redness was established instead by neutering the guard in place (3 failed / 78 passed) and restoring it (0 failed / 81 passed) without touching the fixture. `sends before it stamps` carries no verdict and is an unknown, neither proven nor toothless.
